name: Krag Peak Traverse

pitch_detail.notes: About 1.5 mi up the East Eagle Trail along the valley floor.
Steep, loose rib between two drainages on the west side. Exposure and big loose blocks; the crux of the day.
Cross the crest between the two tops of the double summit; the east summit is the higher.
Follow the ridge, then drop rubbly, loose slopes toward Crater Lake.
pitch_detail.pitch: Crest and descent to Crater Lake

pitch_detail.notes: Little Kettle Creek Trail down many switchbacks to the East Eagle Trailhead.

descent_text: From the east summit, follow the ridge crest and then descend rubbly, loose slopes toward Crater Lake. At the lake, join the Little Kettle Creek Trail (#1945) and follow it down more than 25 switchbacks, through open, sun-exposed slopes that can be overgrown in places, back to the East Eagle Trailhead.
approach: From the East Eagle Trailhead, follow the East Eagle Trail (#1910) up the East Fork Eagle Creek valley for about 1.5 mi to where the route leaves the trail and heads right, up the steep basin on Krag Peak's west side.
overview: A steep, off-trail loop over both summits of Krag Peak, a double-topped peak in the southern Wallowas that rises about 4,500 ft above East Fork Eagle Creek in roughly a mile. You climb a loose rib on the west side to the lower west summit, cross to the higher east summit, follow the crest, and drop to Crater Lake to return by trail. The scrambling is Class 3 on loose rock with some exposure; the trail miles at either end are straightforward.
beta: Walk the East Eagle Trail up the valley for about 1.5 mi, then leave it and head right into the steep basin on Krag Peak's west side. The line climbs the loose, steep rib that divides two prominent drainages; stay on the crest of the rib rather than in the gullies either side. Expect sections of exposure with big loose blocks, and test every hold. The rib tops out on the west (northwest) summit. From there, traverse the crest to the slightly higher east summit, then continue along the ridge crest before descending the rubbly slopes toward Crater Lake. From the lake, pick up the Little Kettle Creek Trail and follow its many switchbacks back down to the East Eagle Trailhead.
gear: Sturdy approach shoes or boots with good edging
Map and compass or GPS for the off-trail section
